classification.difficultyReason: Select suitable points on the supplied fitted line to derive its equation, substitute and rearrange for predictions, then identify interpolation and extrapolation using the appropriate observed variable ranges. The parts explicitly guide this taught sequence.

content.prompt: In an all-female class of Year 10 students, the length of each student’s tibia (shin bone) and height (in centimetres) was recorded and graphed below. A line of best fit was drawn.

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise question 7, scatterplot between the stem and parts
spec.description: Editable reconstruction of the 24 visible red observations, supplied blue fitted line, rectangular grid, labelled axes and lower-left broken-axis cue. Observation coordinates are approximate readings from source pixels. Increased width retains all 17 horizontal tick labels.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal ticks 30–46 in steps of 1; vertical ticks 140–190 in steps of 5. The supplied line is represented by h=2.5t+72.5 over approximately 30.9≤t≤45.2.
spec.answerVisibility: Observations and fitted line are permanent givens. The equation and selected calculation points are not printed on the question graph.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Determine the equation of the line of best fit.

answer.short:
$h=2.5t+72.5$, where $h$ is height in centimetres and $t$ is tibia length in centimetres.

Use two well-separated points on the supplied line to find its gradient.
answer.worked:
Let $t$ be tibia length and $h$ be height, both in centimetres. Read approximately $(31,150)$ and $(45,185)$ from the fitted line.

$$\begin{aligned}m&=\frac{185-150}{45-31}\\m&=\frac{35}{14}\\m&=2.5\end{aligned}$$

Using point–gradient form:

$$\begin{aligned}h-150&=2.5(t-31)\\h-150&=2.5t-77.5\\h&=2.5t+72.5\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the equation to predict the height of a Year 10 female with tibia length of 44 cm.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use the equation to predict the tibia length of a 145 cm tall Year 10 female.

answer.short:
$29\text{ cm}$.

Substitute the height and solve for tibia length.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}145&=2.5t+72.5\\72.5&=2.5t\\t&=\frac{72.5}{2.5}\\t&=29\end{aligned}$$

The predicted tibia length is $29\text{ cm}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Are these predictions examples of interpolation or extrapolation? Explain your answer.

answer.short: (b) Interpolation: $44\text{ cm}$ is within the observed tibia lengths. (c) Extrapolation: $145\text{ cm}$ is below the observed heights.
answer.worked:
In (b), the given tibia length of $44\text{ cm}$ lies within the observed range of approximately $31$–$45\text{ cm}$, so the prediction is interpolation.

In (c), the given height of $145\text{ cm}$ lies below the observed height range of approximately $148$–$185\text{ cm}$, so the prediction is extrapolation.
